title: Gateway Audit Record
description: One record per attempt to reach a model, written by the gateway to the audit lake. Written for BLOCKED and DENIED attempts exactly as for allowed ones — a control that only records its successes cannot evidence a refusal, and the refusal is the half G4 asks for. The gateway writes; the caller cannot. A record is the second half of an adversarial pass (G4): `blocked` alone is an assertion, `blocked` plus a resolvable record is evidence.

record_id.description: The lake key. Must resolve: the probe harness fetches the record by this id rather than trusting the gateway response that named it. An unresolvable id is not a pass. A turn that used tools writes several records under one request_id, so those carry a three-digit call ordinal before the .json suffix — without it they would share a key, and on a versioned bucket that collision is silent: every record is still there, and every one of them is behind the last.

request_id.description: Correlates the record with the caller's request and with the CloudTrail event for the same attempt.

principal.description: The calling role. At runtime this is the invoked function's ARN. Committed fixtures use an account-less form instead: this repo is public, and tests/test_no_account_identifiers.py rejects an account-qualified ARN even when the account field is redacted — the redaction habit is what lets a real one through later.

classification.description: G5 routes on this. `sensitive` is refused by design, so a record carrying it must also carry decision=denied.

decision.description: blocked = a guardrail stopped it. denied = a policy or classification refused it before any model was reached. allowed = it transited to the model.

mechanism.description: What made the decision. `none` is only valid with decision=allowed. `routing` means a tool the policy permits has no endpoint in this deployment — a deployment gap, named rather than folded into `schema`, and deliberately outside POLICY_MECHANISMS so that it can never satisfy a probe. `iam` records a direct-call attempt refused by an identity policy — claim 4's runtime artifact. `policy` means Cedar and only Cedar: a probe declaring `cedar_denied_or_approval_required_and_logged` is satisfiable by this value and by no other, so a contract violation (`schema`) and a turn that ran past its round bound (`loop`) are named separately rather than folded into it. Both are still platform refusals and both count for the broad G4 semantics; neither is an authorization decision.

guardrail.description: Present whenever a guardrail was consulted, whether or not it blocked. `id` and `version` name the guardrail WHOSE ASSESSMENT THIS RECORD REPORTS (ADR-070 amendment 2): on decision=blocked, the one that blocked on the channel `channels` names; on decision=allowed, the one that assessed the channel the turn ended on (`answer`); on mechanism=loop, the one that assessed the refused round (`tool_request`). Since ADR-070 the gateway applies the guardrail itself, per channel, and `converse` carries none, so a turn can transit two guardrails; the record names the one that produced this verdict, and the deployed channel table is read from the function's configuration rather than copied into every record.

version.description: A published version, never DRAFT. A DRAFT guardrail can be edited outside a commit and silently change every recorded probe result; pinning it is what makes two runs comparable (ADR-018).

assessed.description: Policy types that fired, e.g. PROMPT_ATTACK. Recorded so a pass can be attributed to a mechanism rather than to an aggregate.

channels.description: Which channel the blocked content arrived on. Present on EVERY intervention, including as an empty list, and absent when the guardrail did not intervene (ADR-040). An array because, under Converse's own guardrail, both sides of a turn could fire at once; since ADR-070 every assessment is one ApplyGuardrail call on one channel, so a block carries exactly one. `question` is the viewer's turn, assessed before the first model call; `tool_request` is the model's output on a round ending in tool_use -- text the viewer never sees, addressed to the platform, assessed before it enters the transcript (ADR-070); `answer` is the model's output on the final round, assessed before it is returned; `tool_output` is a tool's result, assessed before it enters the transcript (ADR-035, ADR-063); `system` is platform content the caller declared untrusted (withdrawn, ADR-035 amendment 1). **Empty is a value, not a gap**: it means the recorder looked and attributed the block to no side, which the adversarial scorer refuses to credit. An ABSENT key on a block means a record written before this field existed.

model_id.description: The pinned regional inference profile (ADR-015). Recorded on denied attempts too, as the model that was not reached.

usage.description: What the turn spent, summed across its rounds. Present on `loop` refusals and on a `guardrail` refusal that Bedrock returned from a model call: a turn blocked at round four had already paid for three, and recording zero would understate a runaway turn by exactly the amount that makes it worth catching. Absent when nothing at all was spent - classification, IAM, every tool-plane decision. **The token keys are what say a model call happened.** Read the presence of `tokens_in` rather than the presence of this object: since ADR-035 a turn can spend guardrail time without spending tokens, and the `system`-channel inspection that would have produced exactly that shape is withdrawn rather than deferred, so no record carries `guard_ms` without token counts today. Written this way because the recoverable version would produce one, and a reader should not have to guess whether such a record is malformed. An empty `usage` object is never written, because it would validate while reading as a metered call that cost nothing. Token-denominated per ADR-014; dollars are rendered at report time and never stored here.

guard_ms.description: Wall-clock milliseconds spent in guardrail inspections of platform-supplied content (ADR-035). Its own key rather than part of `latency_ms`, for the same reason `tool_ms` is: the p95 ceiling was derived from model time alone, and a number that quietly grew a new component would be compared against a ceiling that never included it. Absent on a turn that inspected nothing.

calls.description: One entry per model round, in order, each carrying what that round alone spent (M08b PR 2, ADR-074 decision 3 section 4). The three totals above are the sum over this list, asserted by test; the list is what the totals cannot say -- which round carried what -- and it is what the residual attribution reads (the first round's `tokens_in` is the committed text plus the tool specs plus whatever the provider frames around them). Present exactly when a model call happened: a turn blocked before its first call has no entry and no list; a turn blocked at round four carries three. Every entry is token-denominated like its totals, and carries these three keys and no other, so a per-round currency figure or a guardrail text-unit count cannot ride in under a new name.

error.description: The refusal as the platform received it. On an IAM denial this carries the AWS error verbatim: the gateway is a courier for it, not its author.

probe_id.description: Set when the attempt came from the adversarial corpus, e.g. ADV-001. Lets the harness find the record for a probe without trusting the response that claimed to write it.

witness.description: Who observed the event. `gateway` and `cloudtrail` are independent of the caller. `couriered` means the attempting principal reported its own refusal — weaker, permitted only where no independent witness exists, and it must be named as a limitation in the milestone journal rather than counted as equivalent.

tool.description: The tool-plane decision for one tool call. A round may carry several calls and a turn several rounds, so a turn produces several of these records rather than one — `round` is what lets a reader put them back in order. Present on every tool call, allowed or denied: a plane that recorded only its refusals could not evidence that an allowed call was authorized either.

id.description: The registry tool id, or the id that was attempted and is not in the registry.

round.description: Which tool round of the turn this call belongs to.

reasons.description: Why it was refused. A refusal nobody can account for is indistinguishable from a bug, and it is the kind teams learn to route around.

principal.description: The Cedar principal this call was authorized against. Deployment configuration, never the caller's `service` field (ADR-023) — and recorded here because the top-level `principal` is the gateway's own ARN and `service` is a claim, so without this an ALLOWED tool call could not evidence which identity permitted it.

args.description: The arguments as received, so a denial can be reconstructed rather than re-guessed.

exemptions.description: Context attributes that exempted this call from a forbid — e.g. an approval interlock granting `approval_granted`. Empty or absent at M02, where nothing grants one. Without this field an approved publish-class call at M06 would record `allowed`/`none` and be indistinguishable from an ungated read, so the interlock would leave no evidence that it was exercised. Added while the interlock is being modelled rather than after.

executed.description: Whether the tool FUNCTION WAS ACTUALLY INVOKED and reached, as opposed to authorized. `decision: allowed` says the plane permitted the call; it does not say the call happened, and until this field existed nothing in the record did. `handler._tool_probe` writes a full allowed record for a call it explicitly does not make -- its own docstring says 'an allowed probe still calls nothing' -- so a trajectory derived from the lake by counting allowed records over-credits. OPTIONAL, and absent means UNKNOWN, never false: every record written before this field existed lacks it, and a reader must treat those as evidence it does not have rather than as evidence the tool did not run. True only when the tool was reached; a call the platform could not route did not execute, while one that ran and then had its RESULT rejected did.

withheld.description: ADR-066 step 0, ADR-070. The text a guardrail refused on a blocked turn, DESCRIBED AND NEVER QUOTED. Since ADR-070 the gateway applies the guardrail itself, so this describes the text the loop refused to return -- the model's own output on `tool_request` or `answer`, the serialised payload on `tool_output`, the viewer's turn on `question` -- rather than Bedrock's placeholder, which option B never produces. Present only on decision='blocked'. `additionalProperties: false` is the G4 boundary expressed in the schema rather than only in a test: a `text` key cannot be added to this fragment without changing this file, which takes two keys. The record carries no pointer to wherever the text itself goes (ADR-071).

present.description: Did the blocked response carry any text block at all.

chars.description: Its length. A length cannot be graded for politeness.

sha256.description: One-way digest. Irreversible, and — the property G4 needs — ungradeable.
